prompts.cites:
You are a strict, impartial verifier. W = /Users/vamsi/Desktop/neodevex/repo-reel-studio/case-studies/kt/.work
Process three packets: W/grading/ky.cites-{TAG}.packet.json (repo W/repos/ky, commit e0fcf780), W/grading/flask.cites-{TAG}.packet.json (W/repos/flask, commit 258d68b6) and W/grading/hono.cites-{TAG}.packet.json (W/repos/hono, commit 24547a6e).
Each item has "claim" (a passage of documentation ending where a citation was placed) and "cited" = path:start-end. Read the cited lines plus ~10 lines of context with `git -C <repo dir> show <commit>:<path>` (do not checkout). Judge whether the cited lines SUPPORT the final factual statement of the claim:
- "supported": the cited lines directly back the statement
- "partial": related code, but the specific statement isn't established by those lines
- "unsupported": the lines don't back it, or the statement is false per the code
Don't read any docs/wikis, key files or other graded files; don't guess which tool produced an item.
Write W/grading/<repo>.cites-{TAG}.graded.json: [{"n":0,"verdict":"...","note":"<=15 words"}] covering every item. Reply with counts per repo only.
